issues.detail: Product creation, usage-based billing (events, meters), and the Next.js webhook handler are described in prose without runnable code, and the webhook handler uses an undefined `db` object.
Example 2 (CLI license gating) has no runnable code, and Example 1 only covers the checkout route and omits the webhook handler for the subscription flow.

scenarios.name: nextjs-pro-subscription-checkout
scenarios.rationale: B matches the rubric closely: it uses `environment: "sandbox"`, `external_customer_id`, `products`, the `subscription.active` webhook, the success-redirect warning and card 4242. A uses `server: "sandbox"` instead of `environment`, and it builds the link with `customerExternalId`, a parameter it admits it is unsure of, so the checkout-route requirements are only partly met even though its webhook and test-card guidance is good.

scenarios.name: express-webhook-raw-body-handler
scenarios.rationale: Both use validateEvent, WebhookVerificationError, express.raw, handle subscription.active and subscription.revoked via customer.externalId, and return 403 on verification failure; A explicitly notes idempotency in its notes and shows the optional-canceled option, while B only mentions idempotency in a code comment, maps products to plans (extra) and returns 400 for non-verification errors, and adds an unverified caveat.

scenarios.name: cli-license-key-activation-flow
scenarios.rationale: B hits every rubric point (benefit with limit 3, activate with key/organization_id/label, validate with activation_id, no token needed, granted=200, 404=revoked/expired/mismatch) while A omits the explicit 404 semantics, treats failures generically, and adds extra unverified fields like conditions/fingerprint.
